NAM.note: Nothing on AI rules or an authority.
No government body using AI is named.
Startup products for diagnostics and education; no public sector system using them is stated.

facts.fact: Namibia Economist reports that Axon AI is developing an AI-powered system for laboratory diagnostics and Okaluli generative-AI education tools, both entering a 33-month incubation after the Seedr Namibia 2.0 AI Edition Demo Day.

NAM.note: Okaluli targets underserved communities without broadband but it is a startup tool, not a government rural connection programme.
A US$5,000 SAFE investment and Seed Capital Fund of Namibia money are named, but no startup law, strategy or labelling is stated.

facts.fact: Namibia Economist reports that CcHub Namibia hosted the Seedr Namibia 2.0 demo day for nine startup and student teams after weeks of mentorship, with two winners entering a 33-month incubation programme.
